title: Chorded Feedback Portfolio — Mini-Probes & Execution Cheatsheet
body:
Executive summary:

This is a compact synthesis of the last 9 weeks of customer feedback (calls, support threads, field notes) focused on inference economics and reliability patterns. Think of it as a small, instrument-ready portfolio: chords (themes) + mini-probes (experiments and low-risk fixes) we can play quickly to test hypotheses and reduce immediate customer pain.

Why this doc: customers are converging on the same few frictions across hosted and dedicated modes. Instead of another long backlog, this cheat-sheet lists 6 high-leverage asks, quick experiment ideas, estimated effort, and suggested owners. Use for sprint planning or a 2-week targeted bug/probe blitz.

Methodology (how this was built):
- Sources: 23 customer calls (Feb–Apr 2028), top 200 CS tickets filtered for "performance/cost/regression", two product demos, and three account escalations.
- Synthesis approach: affinity mapping -> impact × frequency scoring -> quick-probe selection.
- Confidence: medium-high for top 3 items (repeated patterns across >10 accounts), medium for 4–6.

Top-level chord map (themes):
- String 1: Latency spikes on long-context chat sessions (hosted + dedicated)
- String 2: Unclear cost drivers for multi-turn chat (customers surprised by token attributions)
- String 3: KV/prefix cache miss behavior and stale cache confusion
- String 4: Embeddings variance across model variants (customers seeing quality drift after quant updates)
- String 5: Onboarding friction: sample prompts/guardrails for production rollouts
- String 6: Observability gaps: token-level cost traces hard to map to higher-level business metrics

Representative customer quotes (verbatim clips):
- "We thought the session cache would keep costs down on our chat flows — but costs spiked when history hit 4k tokens." — mid-market fintech
- "Why does our dedicated cluster suddenly use a different throughput profile after an auto patch? We need predictable outputs." — large enterprise platform
- "The embeddings similarity changed after the last model swap. Our rerank confidence dropped and users noticed." — e-comm analytics startup

Priority asks and play-by-play (6 items):

1) Fastkv: Cache visibility + conservative fallback policy (Priority: P0)
- What customers say: cache hit/miss patterns are opaque; unexpected fallbacks to full evals cause token surges.
- Hypothesis: exposing cache hit rates + a conservative fallback toggle will prevent surprise cost spikes.
- Mini-probe: add a per-session cache-hit metric to Console (new chart) + a "family-level conservative fallback" boolean canary for 10% of traffic on a few accounts.
- Quick UX: tooltip explaining "fallback reasons" when cost per request jumps.
- Effort: small-medium (dashboard + policy switch), Owner: eng-serving-runtime + Console PM.
- Metrics to watch: per-session token delta, cache-hit rate, downstream token cost, support ticket volume.

2) Token-attribution explainer + example billing breakdowns (Priority: P0)
- What customers say: bills are confusing for multi-turn chat and streaming.
- Mini-probe: ship a sample billing breakdown micro-page in Console for 3 customers showing: prompt tokens, response tokens, KV cache delta, pre- and post-quantization footprint.
- Effort: small (doc + UI sample), Owner: product-hosted-api + finance liaison.

3) Embedding-stability digest + rollback signal (Priority: P1)
- What customers say: embedding distribution shifts after model variant swaps or quant changes.
- Mini-probe: add an automated "embedding drift digest" that runs monthly on a customer's canonical dataset (20–50 samples) and reports cosine shifts vs baseline.
- Effort: medium (batch job + UI), Owner: applied-ml + optimize.
- Quick win: for major drifts, auto-suggest rolling back to previous model for 24–48 hours and alert CS.

4) Latency tail certificates + lightweight SLA guide (Priority: P1)
- What customers say: spikes in 99th percentile latency around long contexts cause timeouts and retries.
- Mini-probe: create a "tail certificate" export that shows 50/90/95/99 latency by session-length bucket for the last 7 days and a lightweight guide recommending configuration knobs (batching, conservative fallback).
- Effort: small, Owner: observability + SRE.

5) Onboarding prompt kit and production sanity checklist (Priority: P2)
- What customers say: early-stage teams ship models with risky prompt patterns (costly long context) or lack guardrails for hallucination.
- Mini-probe: publish a 1-page kit in Console and CS playbook: recommended prompt patterns, sample guardrails, simple eval-set suggestions, suggested safety hooks.
- Effort: small, Owner: developer-experience + CS.

6) Per-route cost attribution labels for Console (Priority: P2)
- What customers say: they want to map feature -> route -> cost to judge ROI per product feature.
- Mini-probe: allow metadata labels on routes in Console and show aggregated cost per-label over selectable windows.
- Effort: medium, Owner: console-and-rollouts.

Low-risk quick fixes (can be done in 1–2 sprints):
- Add a prominent note next to "Deploy model" explaining KV caching behavior and expected token delta on cold-starts.
- Add a CS-runbook snippet that customers can copy into their onboarding doc explaining how to trigger a partial model rollback.
- Prioritize a small ticket to show per-request model-variant in logs to speed up debugging.

Open questions & risks:
- Data privacy: automated embedding-drift digest runs on customer sample data; need legal OK for retention and processing. (Action: legal review)
- Canary surface: exposing a "conservative fallback" might change how we autoscale; SRE must sign off on cost/throughput tradeoffs.
- False positives: embedding drift signal might be noisy for small datasets. Need a threshold strategy.

Suggested owners & timeline (next 6 weeks):
- Week 0–1: finalize success metrics + pick 3 pilot accounts (CS + Solutions) -> Owner: Maya (CS) + Jonas (Solutions)
- Week 2–3: implement Fastkv visibility + sample billing page + tail certificate export (thin MVP) -> Owner: eng-serving-runtime + observability
- Week 4–6: pilot embedding digest on 3 accounts, measure drift noise -> Owner: applied-ml

Measurement & signals of success:
- 30% reduction in surprise billing tickets for pilot accounts within 30 days
- 20% fewer latency-driven retries after tail certificate-driven optimizations
- Early warning: embedding drift digest triggers are actionable in >50% of pilot cases

Notes to product + engineering (raw, stand-ins):
- "If we ship the Fastkv chart, make the default sample window 24h but allow 7d/30d. Keep lightweight." — Jonas
- "Embeddings job should run offline so we don't add 1 more realtime burden. Use customer's canonical sample set they can upload." — Priya
- "We should be careful calling anything an SLA here; call it a 'tail certificate' instead." — Liam

Next steps (actionable):
- CS: pick pilot accounts and collect canonical prompt/embedding sample sets (due: 2028-04-18).
- Eng: scope dashboard mocks + plan for a conservative fallback boolean with SRE (due: 2028-04-22).
- Legal: review embedding digest data processing (due: 2028-04-20).

Appendix — quick references and scratch bits (raw extraction):
- Slack snippet (acct-small-biz): "last week cost exploded when history grew — we didn't realize the cache fallback happened on rehydration"
- Support ticket sample: CS-11209 — billing spike correlates with model variant change, user asked for breakdown.
- Confluence link (internal): Field Chords master note (see linked artifacts)

Rough TODO checklist (for sprint):
- [ ] Draft Fastkv chart spec (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] UI copy for billing breakdown (owner: product-hosted-api)
- [ ] Tail certificate CSV export (owner: observability)
- [ ] Embedding digest pilot plan (owner: applied-ml)
- [ ] Legal signoff request for sample processing (owner: CS)

End of notes. Keep this light and operational — intended to be a living doc updated after each pilot.

-- Maya (CS)
